newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend loss, seen rebounding.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend loss, seen rebounding.

text.p: Polish shares fell for the fourth session running on Tuesday amid Czech currency crisis and falling zloty as well as a busy Polish primary market but analysts saw them rebounding or at least stabilising.
The main market's WIG index fell 0.9 percent, to 15,751.7, and turnover fell 9.4 percent to 118.6 million zlotys ($36.9 million) on all three markets as 67 issues fell, 20 rose and 15 were flat.
Analysts said falling turnovers signalled investors were reluctant to sell at current prices and said the 4.5-percent fall since Wednesday last week was likely to spur some demand.

"There are limits to the falls, low turnover suggests investors don't accept current prices to sell...I think there shouldn't be more falls (on Wednesday)," said Kamil Kalemba, a trader at ING Barings.

Some analysts said the fallout of the Czech currency crisis which hit the zloty made some investors more cautious about buying shares in the whole region. A lot would depend of the way the Polish central bank will handle the problem, they said.
Analysts said Poland's strong fundamentals should prevent falls below 15,500 in the next few weeks, unless the zlotys keeps tumbling. The zloty fell 2.5 percent since Thursday.

Analysts said primary market, where Poland's largest Bank Handlowy was offering shares worth about one billion zlotys in individual and instututional tranches was additionally hurting the bourse prices.
But they said Handlowy's bourse entry in late June could help the bourse in longer-term by boosting the exchange's liquidity, which was likely to attract new capital.
